label: Sequence started with digit 1: late original steps (t>=4) through <DEL>
explanation: Fires when the first original token was the digit 1. Within such sequences it turns on around step 3-4 (step 3 is weak or inactive) and stays active for the rest of the original phase and on the <DEL> step. It switches off immediately in the copy phase, including the step that outputs that leading 1 (only 8 copy-phase activations). It never fires at t<3. Strongest activations come when the sequence starts 1 1 and are at orig_idx 4-6; it fades on later original steps and at <DEL> in long sequences. Activation level does not depend on which token is input at the current step. Weak (<0.3 of max) activations also appear when 1 is the second original token (x 1 ...); these hold about 4% of activation mass and are not covered. On sequences that start with any other token it is essentially silent.

issues: Test numbers reproduce: P 0.994, R 0.731, F1 0.842, mass recall 0.943. Correlation is 0.937. The predicate covers 100% of the top two activation quartiles but only 8.9% of the bottom quartile.

The missed 27% of active steps (5.7% of mass) breaks into three weak classes. (a) orig(0)!=1 & orig(1)==1: 11.5% of active steps, 2.8% of mass, precision 0.16 at t>=4. (b) t==3 onsets when orig(0)==1: 7% of active steps, 2% of mass, precision 0.33. (c) Sequences with no 1 at all: 7% of active steps but only 0.7% of mass, precision 0.001. The explanation names (a) and (b) but not (c). (c) is scattered tiny noise, so 'essentially silent' is still fair by mass.

Checked claims: activity at t<3 is exactly 0. Copy-phase activity is 8 steps, and orig(0)==1 & phase==2 has ~0 recall. Extending the predicate to t>=3 gives test precision 0.845, matching the claimed 0.85. Adding orig(1)==1 drops precision to ~0.58, matching the claimed 0.59. Per-token rates for in_tok are flat at 0.9-1.2x.

The magnitude-fade claim holds only partly. Mean activation per active step is 1.42 (relative units) at orig_idx 4-6 versus 1.37 at orig_idx>=7, so the fade on late original steps is slight. The fade at <DEL> in long sequences is real: 0.73 for L>=8 versus 1.12 for L<=6.
I found no systematic false-positive class: there are only 367 false positives, scattered.
